modern: You will set little value on pleasing song and dancing and the pancratium if you break the melody of the voice up into its separate sounds and ask yourself, of each one, whether you are mastered by this; for you will be stopped by shame from admitting it. And in the case of dancing, do the same with each movement and pose; and likewise in the case of the pancratium. In all things, then, except virtue and the acts of virtue, remember to turn to their separate parts, and by this division come to value them little: and apply this rule to your whole life as well.
original: Thou wilt set little value on pleasing song and dancing and the pancratium, if thou wilt distribute the melody of the voice into its several sounds, and ask thyself as to each, if thou art mastered by this; for thou wilt be prevented by shame from confessing it: and in the matter of dancing, if at each movement and attitude thou wilt do the same; and the like also in the matter of the pancratium. In all things, then, except virtue and the acts of virtue, remember to apply thyself to their several parts, and by this division to come to value them little: and apply this rule also to thy whole life.
